notes: Causal channel: price -> per-user daily subscribe probability, via a log-linear elasticity. After the price hike, each user in the subscriber pool has their daily subscribe probability multiplied by `true_post_subscribe_prob_multiplier` (~0.84). The TRUE counterfactual is generated by re-running the DGP without the price hike (and without the anticipation bump, which would not have happened without an announced change), using the SAME random thresholds — so the difference is purely structural, not noise. `true_ate_on_conv_rate` is the realized observed-minus-counterfactual gap averaged over the post period — this is what an analyst SHOULD recover. A `conv_rate_cf` column is also available in daily_aggregates_intervention.csv for direct comparison. Smooth confounders (secular trend, seasonality) are intended for an ITS model to capture; rough confounders (anticipation, news shocks) are the realism gap an ITS model usually misses.
